thread:
Alex (sales): Hey team — Novara Health wants a Private deployment handoff. Key asks: preserve client source IPs for logging, support split-tunnel SD-WAN to avoid backhauling, and minimal firewall rule set. They also asked for rough PrivateLink vs peering cost tradeoffs for a POC. Can we outline options?
Sam (netops): @Alex quick Q — is Novara going cross-account (their VPC -> our private deploy VPC) or co-account?
Alex (sales): Cross-account. They prefer keep their app in their VPC and call our service via Private connectivity.
Julia (solutions): For cross-account the two common patterns: VPC Peering (or Transit GW) vs AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint -> NLB). Short summary: peering preserves source IP and routing is native, but requires route table entries and CIDR planning. PrivateLink isolates by design, simpler routing, but source IP is not preserved (appears as endpoint ENI).
Sam (netops): Important: PrivateLink will NAT to the endpoint ENI — so backend sees endpoint IPs, not original client IPs. If Novara needs true source-IP for e.g. IP-based allowlists or auditing, peering is the safe option.
Michael (eng): Another option if they must use PrivateLink: have their side send X-Forwarded-For and our app consume that for logs, or put an NLB + Proxy that preserves/proxies client IP (but that adds a hop and operational burden).
Alex (sales): They explicitly called out SIEM ingest requirements (need client IP) and policy that only service owner can view customer IPs. They'd prefer not to change app headers if possible.
Julia (solutions): Then recommend VPC Peering or Transit Gateway. For on-prem split-tunnel, traffic destined for our service should be routed over the SD-WAN to their VPC (or TGW) — avoid hairpin to internet.
Sam (netops): Firewall / security group checklist for peering path (suggested minimal):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from Novara app subnets -> Redwood service subnets
- Allow inbound TCP 443 on Redwood service SG from Novara CIDR(s)
- NTP (UDP 123) if they need time sync (optional)
- DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to their resolver or provide forwarding
```
Sam (netops): Also ensure no overlapping CIDRs. If overlap, must use PrivateLink or NAT/hairpin workarounds.
Alex (sales): Pricing question from Novara: how does PrivateLink billing compare to peering?
Julia (solutions): Rough notes for customer-facing guidance (non-billing legal):
- VPC Peering: no data-processing charges inside AWS between two VPCs in same region, but standard cross-NAT/EIP/egress costs may apply if transit through IGW. Simpler and usually cheaper for high-volume internal traffic.
- PrivateLink: charged per endpoint hour + data processing per GB. For POC light traffic it’s fine, but at sustained high GB/s peering is usually cheaper.
Michael (eng): I'll pull region-specific numbers for the POC and send a short cost table to Novara (estimate per TB).
Alex (sales): Security questionnaire item: Novara wants confirmation on TLS termination policies and TLS inspection. They said their InfoSec might require TLS inspection for egress traffic.
Sam (netops): Note: If we terminate TLS at our service (we own the certs), their TLS inspection likely runs before traffic hits the SD-WAN -> so split-tunnel + on-prem TLS-inspect is their responsibility. If they inspect and re-encrypt, SNI might not be available unless the inspector preserves it. PrivateLink is purely L3/L4; TLS content is end-to-end between their client and our service unless we terminate.
Julia (solutions): If they need to preserve SNI for routing to multi-tenant hostnames, call it out — TLS-inspect devices sometimes remove/alter SNI which breaks Host-based routing. Recommend a short note to their SecOps: do not strip SNI, or use mutual TLS and cert pinning for stronger posture.
Alex (sales): Action items: 1) Sam: provide minimal SG/NACL example and CIDR guidance. 2) Michael: region cost estimate for peering vs PrivateLink for POC (1TB / month). 3) Julia: draft a one-pager pros/cons for Novara SecOps explaining source-IP tradeoffs and TLS-inspect caveats.
Sam (netops): SG snippet for Novara (they run in 10.10.0.0/16, our service in 172.20.0.0/16):
```
# Novara outbound rule (their VPC)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-novara-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 172.20.0.0/16 --description "to Redwood service"
# Redwood inbound rule
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-redwood-svc --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.10.0.0/16 --description "from Novara app"
```
Sam (netops): Also recommend a health-check port for the LB (TCP 8000) if they want active checks over peering.
Michael (eng): I'll put the cost numbers into a quick CSV and ping Novara by EOD.
Julia (solutions): I'll draft the SecOps note and include a suggested Q for their security questionnaire: "Will TLS inspection devices preserve SNI and X-Forwarded-For headers?"
Alex (sales): Perfect. Novara also asked for the POC timeline: can we target network cutover + smoke tests within 2 weeks of their VPN config?
Sam (netops): 2 weeks is doable for peering + route tables + SGs if they provide CIDRs and VPN details this week. PrivateLink is faster to stand up but remember the source IP limitation.
deploy-bot: Deployment reminder — create an internal ticket: NETOPS-4592 (Novara POC network handoff)
Alex (sales): Thanks all — I'll collect Novara's VPN / SD-WAN CIDRs and loop in their SecOps. Will follow up with the one-pager + cost estimate."
